713ebd715f3fcd32: JASIN: Barisan Nasional candidate for the Rim seat, Datuk Khaidirah Abu Zahar, today told her side of the story over allegations that she had used government machinery and facilities for her election campaign in the Melaka election.

She denied any involvement in a Deepavali aid distribution programme organised by the Jasin Municipal Council (MPJ), saying she was neither informed nor invited to the event held at the Rim State Assembly Development and Coordination Committee (Japerun) premises here on Sunday.

Khaidirah, better known as Dira, said she was at the premises to observe the postal ballot verification process for the Rim constituency, involving 180 voters, which was held at the same venue as the Deepavali aid distribution programme
"My presence at the Japerun Rim premises was solely to observe the postal ballot verification process for the Rim state constituency," she said in a statement.
Khaidirah added that candidates were permitted to observe certain postal voting proceedings under the Elections (Postal Voting) Regulations 2003.
"After the postal ballot verification process was completed, I used the toilet facilities at the premises.
"Then, several members of the public approached and greeted me, and I responded as I normally would when meeting residents.
"These interactions were spontaneous and brief, without any prior arrangement or intention to solicit votes," she said.
She also denied claims that she had imposed political conditions on aid recipients or instructed anyone to use the Deepavali programme to promote her candidacy.
Khaidirah said the programme was understood to be part of MPJ's annual festive assistance initiatives, coordinated through local councillors and village heads.

Addressing allegations involving an MPJ officer wearing a shirt featuring her illustrated portrait and the words "Dira Abu Zahar" and "Rim DiHatiku", she said the attire had been produced during her tenure as Rim assemblyman.
She said the shirt was designed for the Wakil Rakyat Untuk Rakyat (WRUR) community programme and distributed to nearly 5,000 people during her previous term.
"The illustration of my face was generated using artificial intelligence (AI), and the shirt was not specifically designed for the 2026 Melaka election campaign.
"It does not feature the BN logo, any political party logo or voting symbol for the current election," she said.
Khaidirah added that she had never instructed the MPJ officer or any civil servant to wear the shirt to campaign for her or solicit electoral support.

She said she respected election laws and the separation between government administration and political activities, adding that the relevant authorities should determine whether any regulations had been breached.
Yesterday, it was reported that Pakatan Harapan (PH) had lodged a police report against Khaidirah over allegations that she had misused government machinery and premises while campaigning.

The report, lodged at the Jasin district police headquarters by PH representative Siti Aishah Shaik Ismail, included allegations involving the use of the JAPERUN Rim Complex for a Deepavali aid presentation ceremony, food baskets bearing the MPJ logo and the presence of MPJ uniformed personnel displaying the candidate's image.
When met by reporters, Khaidirah said the police report would not affect her campaign but expressed disappointment that the allegations had dragged aid recipients into the controversy.
"It does not affect me personally, but when it begins to affect the people in my constituency, that is when I become concerned.
"I am disappointed with the actions of the opposing party. The contest is between the two of us, so there is no need to drag ordinary people into it or make their lives difficult," she said.
She said recipients who had attended the programme in good faith should not have to face unnecessary difficulties because of political disputes.
"These are people who came to receive festive contributions with good intentions.
"Some work shifts, have limited time or face difficulties travelling. Some may not even have their children around to take them from one place to another.
"What may seem like a simple process to others could be burdensome for them," she said.

Khaidirah added that the controversy had not disrupted her campaign activities, which would continue as usual. She also said she had already extended her full cooperation to the police investigation.story, event

1ebc1a4f55c227f3: PETALING JAYA: Bank Negara (BNM) diminta menjelaskan sama ada terdapat garis panduan khusus mewajibkan syarikat insurans memberikan alasan bertulis, bukti dan hak rayuan sebelum seseorang doktor dikeluarkan daripada panel tanpa tunai.
Bekas perdana menteri, Ismail Sabri Yaakob (BN-Bera), menyahut kenyataan Persatuan Perubatan Malaysia (MMA) bahawa dianggarkan sekitar 190 doktor pakar telah kehilangan kemudahan tanpa tunai.
Katanya, jumlah itu amat membimbangkan kerana akhirnya pesakit terjejas dari segi akses dan kelangsungan rawatan.

"Saya dimaklumkan terdapat doktor pakar yang dikeluarkan daripada kemudahan tanpa tunai sehingga ada kes di mana pesakit yang sedang menjalani pembedahan terpaksa dihentikan kerana doktor yang bertugas tidak mempunyai kemudahan tanpa tunai sehingga doktor dari hospital lain terpaksa dipanggil," katanya pada perbahasan Belanjawan 2027 peringkat jawatankuasa bagi Kementerian Kewangan.

Kemudahan tanpa tunai membolehkan pesakit berinsurans menerima rawatan tanpa perlu membuat pembayaran pendahuluan, di mana syarikat insurans akan menjelaskan bil perubatan yang diluluskan secara terus kepada penyedia perkhidmatan kesihatan.
Pada 22 Okt lalu, MMA mendesak BNM menyatakan perlindungan yang tersedia bagi pesakit yang terkesan akibat tindakan syarikat insurans menarik balik kemudahan tanpa tunai untuk pakar perubatan swasta.

Presiden Dr Sivanaesan Letchumanan juga menggesa BNM mendedahkan jumlah aduan yang diterima berhubung sekatan kemudahan tanpa tunai, penarikan balik panel, dan tuntutan agar doktor memulangkan pembayaran, serta berapa banyak kes yang telah diselesaikan.

Desakan ini menyusuli pendedahan di Dewan Rakyat semasa perbahasan Belanjawan 2027, bahawa kira-kira 190 doktor pakar sektor swasta dilaporkan telah kehilangan kemudahan tanpa tunai dengan syarikat insurans.
Nyatakan kriteria syarikat insurans

Dalam ucapannya, Ismail ingin tahu apakah kriteria yang digunakan oleh syarikat insurans untuk mengeluarkan seseorang doktor pakar daripada panel tanpa tunai -- adakah atas dasar prestasi klinikal, isu etika, kelemahan dokumentasi atau semata-mata pertimbangan komersial.
"Jika atas alasan komersial, apakah jaminan bahawa doktor tidak dipilih atau diketepikan secara sewenang-wenangnya tanpa penilaian yang telus dan adil?" soalnya.

"Selain itu, di manakah hak pesakit yang membayar premium insurans setiap bulan kerana apabila mereka jatuh sakit, pihak insurans seolah mengatur pilihan doktor dalam senarai mereka tanpa mengikut prinsip yang ditekankan oleh Majlis Perubatan Malaysia iaitu 'melindungi hak memilih doktor'. Adakah prinsip ini dipatuhi oleh syarikat insurans dan apakah tindakan BNM setakat ini?"
Audit syarikat insurans perlu kawal selia

Sementara itu, Ismail memberitahu Dewan Rakyat bahawa beliau difahamkan syarikat insurans telah melaksanakan audit retrospektif terhadap tuntutan yang telah diluluskan, dan mahu proses itu dikawal selia.

"Saya tidak menafikan hak syarikat insurans untuk menjalankan audit, namun proses ini perlu dikawal selia bagi mengelakkan penyalahgunaan, khususnya melibatkan akses kepada rekod perubatan pesakit yang bersifat sulit dan sensitif," katanya.

"Malah, terdapat hospital yang diminta membayar semula tuntutan dan memberikan diskaun bagi mengelakkan tindakan depanelment, sementara doktor pakar turut kehilangan kemudahan tanpa tunai. Adakah BNM mengetahui dan memantau amalan ini?"

Dalam pada itu, Ismail mendakwa sistem kos perubatan, borang, proses kelulusan awal dan kadar bayaran insurans belum bergerak seiring teknologi perubatan yang semakin maju, seperti pembedahan robotik.
Ismail berkata beliau tidak mahu melihat doktor dan pesakit terpaksa menanggung akibat daripada sistem yang masih ketinggalan ketika teknologi semakin maju.
"Jika sistem sendiri tidak menyediakan pilihan yang tepat, adakah wajar doktor dipersalahkan hanya kerana terdapat kekeliruan dalam pengisian borang?" soalnya.
Ismail mengakhiri perbahasannya dengan mencadangkan BNM bersama Kementerian Kesihatan menetapkan protokol dan kerangka jelas bagi sekatan panel, surat jaminan dan rawatan berterusan.
Beliau juga mencadangkan badan profesional dan industri insurans menyemak kod diagnosis serta prosedur perubatan secara berkala seiring kemajuan teknologi.
386df46eb013ab34: TEHERAN: Iran unveiled a massive billboard and banners pledging to kill US President Donald Trump across Teheran on Tuesday, bringing to a new level the official rhetoric displayed in the capital.
"We will kill Trump", read the billboard towering over the busy Enghelab Square in Teheran, which depicted the US president behind bars with his head bowed.

New designs of billboards and displays mocking and vowing revenge against Trump have frequently been set up around Teheran since the war began on Feb 28 when US-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

In recent days, renewed diplomatic efforts have been underway to bring Teheran and Washington to negotiate to prevent a resumption in fighting which has spread across the region and driven prices up globally.
Trump, who on Tuesday faces crucial US midterm elections amid voter discontent driven in part by the Iran war, has said that a deal "could happen."

In the busy Tajrish Square in northern Teheran, an open-air exhibition featured paintings of Trump, including one showing him with his face lying bloodied on the ground as a foot presses down on his head.
Another depicted a bomb obscuring his face, in an apparent reference to Belgian surrealist Rene Magritte's 1964 painting "The Son of Man."

Nearby, a life-sized replica of a jail cell has remained on display, with an actor impersonating Trump spending the day inside. An adjacent screen showed images of the damage caused by US strikes on Iran.
Teheran accuses Trump of deliberately targeting civilian sites during the war, including a school and a wedding ceremony, killing dozens of people including women and children.

State-sponsored billboards and murals have been a fixture of Iran's public spaces since the 1979 Islamic revolution, used to honour allies, celebrate military figures and send political messages to adversaries, particularly the United States and Israel.

ac9cca840060979a: AMSTERDAM: Dutch electronics and medical device manufacturer Philips said Tuesday it had reached a deal "in principle" with US authorities to settle a long-running case over faulty sleep machines.
The company has for years been weighed down by a series of crises over the recall of its DreamStation machines for sleep apnoea, a disorder in which breathing stops and starts during sleep.
Millions of devices were recalled over concerns that users were at risk of inhaling pieces of noise-cancelling foam and fears it could potentially cause cancer.

Presenting its third-quarter (Q3) results, the Dutch firm said it had "reached an agreement in principle with the US justice department to resolve the previously disclosed criminal and civil investigations related to the... recall".
The company set aside €288 million (US$322 million) in Q3 of this year to settle the case, with payment expected in the first quarter of 2027.
"The settlement is subject to finalisation of the relevant documentation," said Philips.
The provision pushed down the company's Q3 profits to €28 million, compared to €187 million in the same period of last year.
Chief executive officer Roy Jakobs told reporters the deal was clinched "in the last few days", but declined to give further details while the paperwork was being finalised.
"It's for sure an important milestone for us as it marks a step forward in resolving the sleep and respiratory care related proceedings," he said.
Market traders appeared to agree, pushing up the stock around six percent at the opening bell.
'AI-enabled innovations'
Once famous for making lightbulbs and televisions among other products, Amsterdam-based Philips in recent years has sold off subsidiaries to focus on medical care technology.
The firm recorded quarterly turnover of €4.4 billion, compared to €4.3 billion in Q3 of 2025.
Philips maintained its forecast of sales growth over the full year of between 3% and 4.5%.
"We delivered a strong Q3," said Jakobs.
"We see our customers responding well to our latest AI-enabled innovations," added the CEO.
In February, Philips posted its first annual profit after three straight years of losses, turning in a better-than-expected gain of €897 million.
In the second quarter of this year, the firm reported net profits of €386 million, helped by a refund from US tariffs later struck down by the US Supreme Court.
Jakobs painted a bright outlook for the firm.
"Our year-to-date results, together with our strong order book, give us confidence in delivering our full-year outlook and achieving our medium-term ambitions," said the executive.

601cfd26de0279b1: Raspberry Pi has announced yet another round of price hikes, this time adding $80 to the cost of its 16GB Pi 5, which now sells for more than three times its original launch price.

The latest bump, announced by Raspberry Pi boss Eben Upton, takes the 16GB Pi 5 to a whopping $385. The 16GB Compute Module 5 variants are also getting $40 more expensive, although the Raspberry Pi 500+, which packs the same amount of RAM, has escaped this particular round.
Upton blamed a familiar culprit: soaring memory costs, worsened by a lack of alternative suppliers for 16GB DRAM and ongoing shortages of other components.

"Unfortunately, a lack of alternative supply for 16GB DRAM, compounded by other ongoing component shortages, means we now need to make further price increases on some of our highest-density products," Upton wrote.

It's becoming an expensive habit for Raspberry Pi customers. The 16GB Pi 5 cost $120 when it launched in January 2025, which seems almost reasonable now. Raspberry Pi added $25 in December, another $60 in February, and a further $100 in April. With today's $80 increase, buyers are being asked to cough up $265 more than they were less than two years ago, a price hike of 221 percent.
And it's barely been a month since Raspberry Pi raised prices on its 2GB Pi 4 and Pi 5 models by $12.50 apiece, taking them to $67.50 and $77.50 respectively.

The repeated markups come despite Raspberry Pi reporting record first-half results in September. Revenue jumped 90 percent to $256.9 million, while gross profit rose 79 percent to $59.4 million. Gross profit per board climbed 53 percent to $12.20, helped partly by memory purchased before prices went through the roof. That stockpile advantage has since largely disappeared.
For customers unwilling to pay nearly $400 for a single-board computer, Upton advises buying something with less RAM, using an older Pi, or optimizing applications to make do with less memory.
He also warned that some sellers are exploiting the shortages by charging inflated prices or offering products that aren't what they appear to be, urging customers to stick to approved resellers.

“We’re aware that a few bad actors have been taking advantage of the current memory supply circumstances to sell Raspberry Pi products at inflated prices or shift products that aren’t what they seem,” he said.

There is, apparently, some good news, as Raspberry Pi continues to insist the increases are temporary. "As we've said from the beginning, the current memory landscape is difficult but ultimately temporary, and we look forward to rolling back our price increases when memory costs fall once again," Upton wrote.
That could be a long wait. Micron has previously warned that memory shortages could drag on into 2028 or beyond, so anyone hoping to see a $120 Pi 5 again probably shouldn't hold their breath. ®

7764fbdd64837c46: JERANTUT: A teacher has been arrested for sexually assaulting a male student several times in a school storeroom.
District police chief Superintendent Noor Azman Yusof said the suspect was a 24-year-old man.
The case came to light after the boy told his father what happened.
A police report was lodged on Oct 27, leading to the teacher's arrest. He has been remanded until tomorrow.
"The case is being investigated under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act," Noor Azman said.
The section relates to sexual assault on a child and carries a maximum jail term of 20 years and caning.
The victim told his father that the teacher had frequently caned him for failing to complete his homework.
The teacher would then take him to a storeroom, order the boy to perform indecent acts on him and sexually assault him.
1329ba9be395653b: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 3 — The ongoing construction of a high-altitude training centre on Mount Kinabalu has come under scrutiny, with indigenous groups and tourism stakeholders questioning its environmental impact, approvals and whether communities with customary ties to the mountain were adequately consulted.

The controversy surfaced around October 30 after photographs showing structures and apparent drilling activities near Sayat-Sayat circulated on social media, prompting calls for authorities to clarify the nature and purpose of the work.

The photographs prompted criticism over a lack of transparency, including from Kundasang Tourism and Culture Association chairman Datuk Japiril Suhaimin, who called for an investigation into the project's location, scope and approvals, as well as its potential effects on water sources, soil stability and biodiversity.

Bundu Tuhan Village Heritage and Culture head Adrian Soros also questioned whether communities with customary ties to the mountain had been consulted, saying many villagers were unaware of the construction.
He raised concerns about drilling into the mountain, which he said went against customary beliefs, as well as the protection of local water sources and the management of human waste at high altitude.

Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin subsequently issued a statement saying the project was not new and had originally been proposed under the Kinabalu Park Development Plan in 2015.
He said the project had obtained approval from the Sabah Parks Board of Trustees and endorsement from the Mount Kinabalu Native Customary Advisory Council.
“The HATC was originally proposed under the Kinabalu Park Development Plan in 2015, but its implementation was deferred following the earthquake that struck Mount Kinabalu that year.

“The initiative was subsequently revived and officially launched in 2025 as part of Sabah’s efforts to diversify its tourism offerings and strengthen its position as an internationally recognised mountaineering destination,” he said.
The new development would provide basic accommodation and specialised facilities to support high-altitude training and mountaineering activities.

Jafry said the centre was intended to cater to mountaineers preparing for expeditions to higher-altitude destinations, including Mount Kilimanjaro, Aconcagua and Mount Everest, by providing facilities for altitude acclimatisation, technical training and familiarisation with specialised climbing equipment.

He said construction involved lightweight, prefabricated and modular building materials to minimise environmental disturbance, with the structures designed to withstand strong winds and challenging weather conditions at higher elevations.
The construction method also avoided the use of heavy machinery in view of the mountain’s sensitive natural environment.

Jafry said the project’s approval and implementation must respect Mount Kinabalu’s cultural and spiritual significance to indigenous communities, as reflected in the involvement of the Native Customary Advisory Council.
The minister nevertheless emphasised that the approval did not exempt the project from complying with stipulated conditions, technical specifications and environmental regulations.

“We take the concerns raised by the public seriously. The ministry will consider a comprehensive investigation to ascertain whether all approved specifications, environmental safeguards and regulatory conditions have been fully observed.
“Should any non-compliance be established, the ministry will not hesitate to pursue the necessary enforcement measures in accordance with the law,” he said.

However, despite his statement, the Dayak International Organisation (DIO) today called for all construction, drilling and installation work at the site to stop, alleging that the development violated indigenous customary law protected under the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP).

Its United Nations representative, Datuk Petinggi Andrew Ambrose Atama Katama, questioned the use of the Mount Kinabalu Native Customary Advisory Council to endorse the project, saying this did not replace the need for consent from communities, particularly the Kadazandusun and Momogun.
Andrew described Aki Nabalu as a sacred living entity and ancestral repository rather than a commercial asset for generating state revenue.

DIO also called for an independent environmental audit, including an assessment of wastewater impact on local water catchments, and said it would raise the matter at the United Nations Permanent Forum on Indigenous Issues and the Unesco Global Geoparks Network.
Mount Kinabalu, also known as Aki Nabalu, is Sabah's highest peak at 4,095 metres and holds deep cultural and spiritual significance for indigenous communities, particularly the Kadazandusun.
Every year, locals hold sacred rituals to honour the mountain spirits, seek permission and protection, and ensure the safety and well-being of climbers.
Kinabalu Park was inscribed as a Unesco World Heritage Site in 2000 for its exceptional biodiversity, including thousands of plant species and a wide range of habitats.

d886f1ddf5fc4c44: PETALING JAYA: Deputy prime minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has denied allegations that he attempted to sabotage the unity government with his remarks on the shelving of several rural development projects in Sabah and Sarawak.
Zahid, who is also rural and regional development minister, insisted that his remarks on the postponement or cancellation of the letters of acceptance (SST) for the projects were accurate.
He also said he was prepared to produce documentary evidence of the official directive to counter the allegations made against him.

“I have no intention to do that (sabotage), but those are the facts... Whether they were postponed or cancelled, what is clear is that all SSTs that have been and are due to be issued were ordered to be cancelled.

“I have evidence of the directive letter that was issued. I can show it to the Jelutong MP,” Bernama reported him as saying at a press conference after officiating an event at Dewan MPJ Alamanda in Jasin, Melaka.
Yesterday, Jelutong MP RSN Rayer accused Zahid of trying to sabotage the unity government with his remarks on the shelving of several rural development projects in Sabah and Sarawak.
Rayer said Zahid made the government seem indifferent to the infrastructural issues faced by the two states as well as rural communities in the peninsula.

He said claims that the funds set aside for the shelved projects had been wasted had angered the public, even though finance minister II Amir Hamzah Azizan had clarified that no projects had been cancelled.
Rayer also alleged that Zahid was conspiring with the opposition to topple the government.

Last week, when winding up the debate on the 2027 budget, Zahid had claimed that projects in Sabah and Sarawak were shelved on the orders of the rural and regional development ministry's secretary-general, despite funds being set aside for it.

Amir later rejected claims the finance ministry had cancelled projects, saying the rural and regional development ministry was merely told to hold off on awarding new road contracts until the unpaid bills were cleared.
57c18b0fbebf2714: KUALA LUMPUR: To a teenage Shalin Zulkifli, she was "Auntie Shirley", the reassuring senior beside whom she felt safe.
To Lydia Kwah, she was a fighter who could still smile under pressure.
To Chong Yew Jin, whose first lesson with her began on his seventh birthday, she became a "second mother".

Shirley Chow, who has died aged 76, won medals for Malaysia and helped younger bowlers find the confidence to pursue their own. In the memories of those she guided, the two achievements are inseparable.

Her honours included the 1979 National Sportswoman of the Year award, an Asian Games gold and a World Championships silver. Behind those achievements was a woman remembered for sharing her knowledge, remaining patient and showing up when her teammates and proteges needed her.
Shirley belonged to the pioneering generation that helped lay the foundations for Malaysia's emergence as a force in women's bowling.
When she became the first female bowler to be named National Sportswoman of the Year in 1979, Shalin was barely one.

By her mid-teens, Shalin was winning international medals beside the woman she called Auntie Shirley. She would become a mainstay of Malaysia's success and receive the same national honour five times — in 1994, 1996, 1997, 2001 and 2002.

Lydia, Lisa Kwan and Sharon Low also followed Shirley onto the national awards roll. Decades later, Natasha Roslan became its sixth female tenpin bowling recipient, earning the 2023 award after winning the world singles title.
For Shalin, the connection between those generations was personal.
"When I bowled with Auntie Shirley, I always felt safe," she recalled.
Shalin was 15 when she won SEA Games trios gold alongside Shirley and Lisa in Singapore in 1993. A year later, she joined Shirley and Lydia to capture the Asian Games trios title in Hiroshima.
In 1995, Shalin, Shirley and Lisa claimed the world trios silver in Reno, United States.
The results became part of Malaysian bowling's history. What stayed with Shalin was the reassurance of having experienced teammates beside her.
"She was a really good senior and teammate because she was never stingy about sharing her experience and knowledge with me," said Shalin.
Shirley did not need to be the loudest person in the team to make her presence felt. Her quiet confidence gave a young bowler room to learn without feeling she had to outshine the seniors around her.
When a difficult game demanded someone step up, Shalin trusted her to be there.
"She taught me patience," said Shalin.
"You can have confidence in yourself, but you don't have to shout it out. Let your results do the talking."
Shalin remembers entering the senior team conscious of how much she had to learn from Shirley, Lydia, Lisa, Karen Lian and the other experienced players.
She regarded being among them as a privilege. She absorbed their advice, adapted it to her own game and, as her career progressed, tried to offer younger teammates the same support.
The lessons went beyond technique. They learned how to remain dependable when things went wrong, how to share knowledge and how to put the team ahead of individual egos.
Lydia's memories of Hiroshima offer a revealing example of how that team spirit was sometimes forged.

She recalled a misunderstanding with Shirley before the doubles competition. The reason has faded from memory, but she remembers coach Sid Allen bringing the players together for a team meeting and helping resolve it.
When he announced that Lydia and Shirley would bowl together, both were surprised.
"Both of our eyes went big," Lydia recalled.
The following day, they put their differences aside.
"We both bowled incredibly well and we surprised the whole team that we won silver medals," she said.
They then joined Shalin for the trios and won gold.
Lydia, who knew Shirley through their shared Ipoh roots, remembers a friendly, kind teammate whose resolve was particularly evident on the lanes.
"Shirley was always a fighter on the lanes. She always had a smiling face, even under pressure," she said.
For Lydia, Shirley's place in the sport's history is assured.
"Shirley Chow is our bowling legend. She helped put Malaysia on the world bowling map."
Shalin also admired the way Shirley found her own route to international success.

She remembers her using a distinctive backup delivery with a light ball, yet competing successfully at the highest levels. Just as significant was Shirley's willingness to continue contributing after leaving the national team.

Back in Ipoh, she devoted her experience to younger bowlers, including those in development programmes and preparing for the Malaysia Games. One of them was a seven-year-old whose family had just moved from Selangor to Perak.
Yew Jin's parents took him bowling on his birthday. Shirley noticed how much he enjoyed the sport and approached them about training him.
"That's when everything started," he recalled.
For the boy who accepted that invitation, Shirley became a constant through much of his life.
He credits her with teaching him the fundamentals and helping him develop his hook. Yet the quality he remembers just as strongly was her patience.
Yew Jin could become frustrated when he bowled poorly. Shirley, he said, never became angry with him. She had a clear ambition for her pupil.
"One thing she always told me was that she was trying to make me a better bowler than her," he said.
"Unfortunately, I'm far from that."
A medal he would eventually bring home to her showed how deeply her lessons had taken root.
After a disappointing outing at the 2022 Sukma, Yew Jin trained hard for the 2024 edition in Sarawak. He wanted Shirley there with him, but his budget was not enough.
During the trios competition, he reached a point where he thought his chance had gone. He began crying before play had finished.
Then he remembered what Shirley had taught him: never give up. The opponents could still have a poor game. There was still a reason to keep bowling.
True enough, Yew Jin scored 255 in his final game, helping him and his two teammates secure bronze. It was, he said, the happiest moment of his life.
"Even though it's only a bronze, for me, it's everything I wanted in bowling."
He later took the medal to Shirley. He wanted her to know how much of it belonged to her — the years of coaching, the patience, and the advice he had remembered when he was close to surrendering.
"I told her she did it. She made me what I am."
Even then, Shirley was still very much a coach. When he showed her videos of his bowling, she continued pointing out how he could improve.
Their conversation also turned to what would come next.
Yew Jin was considering stopping bowling after Sukma to concentrate on his studies and work. Shirley urged him to reconsider.
He remembered her telling him that he could slow down without giving up something he loved.

Her interest in his life extended well beyond the lanes. They talked about his brother's wedding, whether he had a girlfriend, and the ordinary family matters that fill conversations among people who have known each other for years.
"She taught me everything about bowling. In real life, she is like a second mother to me," he said.
That is why the news of her death has been so difficult to absorb.
Yew Jin said he last saw her about a month ago. She was energetic and talking as usual. He had imagined more visits, more conversations and another chance to bring her something he had won.
"I was hoping that I could bring a big trophy back to her."
Shalin, too, carries the sadness of a meeting that did not happen.
Busy with their respective lives, they had not seen each other as often as she would have liked, although they remained connected through a group chat with other former teammates.
She was unable to attend when MTBC officials went to Ipoh last year to present Shirley with the cash incentive attached to her 1979 national award. Shalin regrets not seeing her again.
Her hope now is that younger Malaysian bowlers preserve the qualities Shirley and her generation helped build: generosity, trust and a willingness to put personal feelings aside for the team.
Those values, she believes, helped make Malaysia formidable in international team competition. Carrying them forward is part of honouring the seniors who passed them down.
Shirley's influence could be seen in the support Shalin offered the juniors who followed her, and in a Sukma bowler who found the resolve to finish when he thought he had lost.
Yew Jin had also hoped she would be there for milestones beyond bowling. She had wanted to attend his and his brother's weddings.
"Unfortunately, the seat for her is left unoccupied," he said. The thought of her absence is another measure of how much she meant to him.

bb95bd1d9f6ead5a: KUALA LUMPUR: Fashion Valet Sdn Bhd’s shareholders' agreement required board approval before the company could declare dividends, the sessions court heard today.

Corporate lawyer Anne Wong, 49, who was involved in drafting the agreement dated March 5, 2018, said in her witness statement that the approval had to come from a majority of directors, including those appointed by Pulau Tiga Ventures Sdn Bhd, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Khazanah Nasional Bhd.
Wong was testifying in the RM8 million criminal breach of trust trial involving Fashion Valet founders Vivy Yusof and her husband, Fadzarudin Shah Anuar.

Referring to Clause 7.5.1(ii)(b) of the agreement, she said any declaration of dividends required the approval of a majority of directors, including those appointed by Start Today Co Ltd and Pulau Tiga Ventures.
She also said the Companies Act 2016 prohibited a company from declaring dividends if it did not have profits.

On loans and credit facilities, Wong said Fashion Valet was prohibited from extending them to its directors, shareholders, related companies or other parties without the approval of a majority of the board.
Referring to Clause 7.5.1(ii)(d), she said the approval had to include directors appointed by Start Today and Pulau Tiga Ventures.
“As such, any advances to any party must first obtain the board's approval,” she said.
Wong added that Fashion Valet was required to submit a summary of the utilisation of investment funds to the board every three months and annually until the funds were fully utilised.
She said the company was not required to disclose its entire operational expenditure.
Vivy and Fadzarudin, both 38, were jointly charged on Dec 5, 2024, with criminal breach of trust involving investment funds from Khazanah and Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB).

They are accused of authorising a payment of RM8 million from Fashion Valet’s corporate bank account to 30 Maple Sdn Bhd without board approval on Aug 21, 2018, at Public Bank's Bukit Damansara branch.
The charge, under Section 409 of the Penal Code, carries a maximum jail term of 20 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
They also pleaded not guilty to an alternative charge of dishonestly misappropriating RM8 million in investment funds from Khazanah and PNB belonging to Fashion Valet.
The offence, under Section 403 of the Penal Code, carries a jail term of between six months and five years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
Lawyer Shaarvin Raaj represented the couple, while deputy public prosecutor Nidzuwan Abd Latip appeared for the prosecution.
The trial before judge Rosli Ahmad continues on Nov 20.
688d755bb720eba1: KUALA LUMPUR: Continued forest destruction in Shah Alam is no longer merely an environmental issue but a serious public safety concern, said Pertubuhan Pelindung Khazanah Alam Malaysia (Peka).

Peka president Rajesh Nagarajan said this was reflected in the latest disasters affecting the city, including yesterday's flash floods, which threatened residents' safety and disrupted major transport routes.

The floods also triggered a landslip at a parking area in Subang Permata and forced the closure of both directions of the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE) between Setia Alam and Shah Alam following a river overflow.
"These disasters stem from uncontrolled clearing of forests, hillsides and natural water catchment areas across Shah Alam.
"The destruction at Bukit Cerakah is particularly concerning, with residents raising concerns over clearing activities near Perdana Heights since 2020.
"The 174-hectare Shah Alam Community Forest (SACF), one of the remaining lowland forests in the area, also continues to face encroachment and development threats," he said in a statement today.
Rajesh said Peka and the SACF Association had previously taken legal action to challenge the degazettement of part of the Bukit Cerakah Forest Reserve.

Although the Federal Court dismissed their application for leave to appeal in April, he said the decision did not absolve the Selangor government of its responsibility to protect the remaining forest areas.
"Forests serve as natural defence systems by absorbing rainwater, controlling surface runoff and stabilising hillsides.
"Replacing natural catchment areas with concrete structures leaves downstream communities more vulnerable to flash floods and landslides," he said.
Rajesh said Peka had warned the Selangor government about the dangers on June 20 last year.
"However, 17 months have passed, and Shah Alam is flooded again. How many more warnings must be ignored?" he said.
He added that the authorities were allegedly relying on assurances about the operation of mechanical pumps and the opening of temporary relief centres (PPS) to address the situation.
"Pumps cannot replace the functions of forests, restore destroyed catchment areas or undo the consequences of irresponsible land-use planning," he said.
Peka wants the Selangor government to impose an immediate moratorium on forest clearing and hillside development in environmentally sensitive areas.
It also wants the SACF and the remaining ecologically valuable areas of Bukit Cerakah to be permanently gazetted and protected.
Rajesh further called for an independent public inquiry into the recurring floods in Shah Alam, including the effects of deforestation and development.

He also called on the authorities to disclose all development approvals and Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs) involving forest and water catchment areas. They should also identify those responsible for approving projects that affect forests, hillsides and natural drainage systems.
"The state government should not continue sacrificing forest resources in the name of development, only to express sympathy when residential areas are affected.
"Every tree felled, hillside cleared and catchment area destroyed adds to the burden borne by the people.
"Shah Alam is not merely being submerged by rainwater, but by deforestation, destructive development and political failure," he said.
Media reports said three people, including an elderly man with disabilities and a baby, were evacuated to a PPS following flash floods in Kampung Melayu Subang.

9b404c2ab078ecdc: SINGAPORE, Nov 3 — Reformative training and jail time should be the default sentencing options for scammers and those who facilitate scams, according to a Bill proposed in Parliament on Tuesday (November 3).

The Sentencing (Scams) Bill, introduced by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), reaffirms Parliament's intention that scam and scam-enabling offences should be met with strong deterrent sentences because of the serious harm they cause to victims.
However, on September 10, the High Court published its judgment regarding the case of Mohamed Erzan Taib Zohri, one among six young offenders who allegedly committed scam-enabling offences.
The court allowed four of the six appeals and replaced the offenders' reformative training sentences with probation.

The High Court also held that reformative training or imprisonment should not be the default sentence for young offenders who commit scam-enabling offences. According to MHA, this is inconsistent with Parliament's intention that such offences should generally attract deterrent sentences.

Under the proposed Bill, the High Court's decision will not be binding on and need not be considered by any court when considering any sentence imposed on scam offenders or scam-enabling offences, or when hearing appeals relating to such sentences.

In addition, courts, except the Youth Court, should consider reformative training or imprisonment as the primary and default sentencing options for offenders aged 21 and below, unless there are exceptional circumstances, the Bill states.
Youth offences relating to scams on the rise
Scams remain the most prevalent crime type in Singapore, with an average of 90 scam reports amounting to S$2 million (RM6.4 million) in losses each day in the first half of 2026, MHA said.

Over 1,000 youths were investigated in connection with scam reports in 2025, while the number of youths who committed cheating and related offences rose 37 per cent, from 814 in 2024 to 1,114 in 2025.
These youths were largely involved in scam cases as mules, according to MHA.
“We need to do more to deter young offenders from being enticed by the prospect of quick financial gains to commit such offences,” the ministry stated.
MHA added: “If a deterrent approach is not taken, Singapore's scam and youth offending situation could deteriorate.”
MHA emphasised that scams can cause serious harm to victims and must be met with a strong deterrent message, which the Bill seeks to reinforce. — AsiaOne

32335db8346ea938: BUDAPEST: Hungarian lawmakers are set to elect a new prosecutor-general on Tuesday, part of pime minister Peter Magyar's push to hold nationalist ex-leader Viktor Orban and his allies accountable over alleged corruption.

Three ex-ministers are in custody, including a former central bank governor, whom Orban once called his "right-hand" man.
President Andras Baka has nominated Peter Fejes, a recently retired career prosecutor and former regional chief prosecutor, for the top post.
Magyar's Tisza party, which holds more than two-thirds of parliamentary seats, said it will approve the nominee.
MPs are scheduled to cast their ballots around 11am local time.
'Free from politics'
Public confidence in the prosecution service eroded under Orban's 16-year rule, as critics accused the highly centralised institution of shielding the premier's inner circle from legal scrutiny.
Fejes, 65, said he aimed to regain the lost trust.
"The emphasis must be placed on professionalism, timeliness and being free from politics," Fejes told conservative website Valasz Online last week.
Parliament rejected Baka's first nominee for prosecutor-general last month after reports revealed that his brother was linked to the so-called "golden convoy" case.
Just ahead of April's parliamentary elections - which Orban ended up losing to Magyar - Hungarian security forces stopped transport vehicles of a Ukrainian state-owned bank transiting the country.
They detained seven employees and seized millions of dollars, euros and gold bars.
Hungary's tax authority said it acted in a money-laundering probe, but the detainees were quickly released, the assets returned and the original case was eventually closed.
Meanwhile, a separate inquiry was opened into alleged rights violations during the operation.
In June, the lead prosecutor investigating that case, Pal Furcht, stepped down, later alleging his superiors obstructed his probe and that evidence pointed to Orban ordering the operation.
Lawyer Lorant Horvath, who represents both Furcht and the detained bank employees, said he hoped Fejes would look into the matter.
"Our biggest concern is that the prosecutor-general's office played an active role" in the operation, he told AFP.

Former top prosecutor Gabor Balint Nagy announced his resignation in July after facing pressure from Magyar, who was elected on the promise of "regime change" and has pushed to get rid of a host of top officials appointed under Orban.
Ex-ministers probed
Other investigations have gained momentum since Orban lost power.

Ex-central bank governor Gyorgy Matolcsy, also a former economy minister, was arrested last month over "economic fraud causing particularly significant financial loss", and an international arrest warrant was issued against his son, Adam, a suspected accomplice.
Two other former ministers have been in custody since September over alleged graft, thought to have caused millions of euros of losses in public funds.
Orban denounced the latter two probes as "politically motivated" processes aimed at imprisoning him and destroying his party.
By going after these cases, prosecutors have so far touched "only the bare minimum", Horvath said.
The country's new top anti-graft official, Anna Unger, has warned that getting convictions could take many years.
A government website lists over 60 cases referred to investigators, involving billions of euros in taxpayers' money, with fresh cases added regularly.

70e71dc02cf270c6: SINGAPORE, Nov 3 — The nine-and-a-half hour disruption to public healthcare services on October 13 affected about 4,000 outpatient appointments, said Senior Minister of State for Health Tan Kiat How in Parliament on Tuesday (November 3).
He was responding to questions filed by MPs Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang SMC), Poh Li Sam (Sembawang West SMC), Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar GRC) and Cassandra Lee (Tampines GRC).
They had asked questions ranging from the disruption’s cause, to its impact, and operational resilience plans.
The senior minister of state acknowledged that the disruption caused inconvenience and concern to patients and their families, and created additional work for the country’s healthcare workers.
“We apologise. It should not have happened,” Tan said.
Investigation findings
He reiterated Synapxe’s statement on October 13 that the incident was not a cyberattack and that there was no unauthorised access to, compromise, or loss of patient data.
The incident, he said, was caused by a required security update to a shared domain name system or Domain Name System (DNS) service that was not completed before a scheduled global change.
DNS is akin to the phonebook of the Internet, helping systems locate and connect to applications.
But the incident was avoidable, Tan acknowledged.
“This was a known change and a preventable lapse. Synapxe had contracted a service provider to manage the necessary update, but it was not carried out,” he explained.
The national health technology agency is now reviewing the service provider’s contractual obligations and will take “appropriate action” for any established lapses, Tan said.
The senior minister of state also highlighted that Synapxe remains accountable for the resilience of its critical systems regardless of outsourcing.
He noted that while monitoring had picked up abnormal activity, further time was taken to identify the underlying problem and restore services safely.
To this, he said that Synpaxe is now strengthening monitoring and fault diagnosis to enable faster recovery.
It will also look into shared dependencies and alternative recovery arrangements.
In this instance, while the systems had backup infrastructure, including two data centres, both depended on the same underlying DNS service and security configuration.
This means that switching between the data centres would not have resolved the disruption.
Synapxe will therefore review such shared dependencies and strengthen alternative recovery arrangements, Tan added
The October 13 disruption affected services such as appointment bookings, visitor registration, medication dispensing and billing.

Healthcare institutions had to activate downtime procedures with additional staff supporting operations, and clinicians used selected read-only patient records and manual workflows to continue essential care.
The incident did not result in any known patient safety incidents.
Meanwhile, the Ministry of Health will oversee and verify corrective actions, Tan said.

He added that an expert panel comprising representatives from other organisations that have similar engineering profiles has also been appointed to review the investigation findings and proposed remediation measures and identify further improvements.
“Digitalisation brings important benefits to healthcare, but as our systems become more interconnected, resilience must improve too.
“We must make our technology more reliable while ensuring healthcare workers can continue caring for patients safely, even when technology fails,” Tan said. — AsiaOne
3eb5274e6bf27077: Distributed teams need to collaborate on shared information, but duplicated files, delays, and competing versions keep getting in the way.
Picture a video production team with editors in different cities. One person updates a project file, another keeps working from an earlier copy, and a third waits for a large transfer to finish.
When teams need to collaborate on large files across locations, traditional storage and file-sharing arrangements introduce friction precisely where people expect technology to help.
The hard part isn't merely moving a file. It's knowing who has the authoritative copy, when changes are available, and whether somebody else is still working on an outdated version.

Consider a game studio preparing a build for review. A designer exports an updated asset, but a colleague pulls an older version from a synced folder. The mistake only becomes obvious when the pieces are assembled. The team must trace the mismatch, resend files, and repeat work.

Sync-and-download workflows depend on a chain of uploads, downloads, and decisions about which copy is current. Under deadline pressure, that chain breaks. Delayed access means missed handoffs; duplicated files mean extra checking and sometimes rework.

For IT, each workaround creates another question: where does the data live, who can access it, and how do teams maintain consistent controls? Adding another collaboration application doesn't resolve those underlying questions.
The useful starting point is the workflow. Find out where teams copy data, where they wait, and what prompts them to work outside the shared system.

These frustrations cut across industries, but the ways organizations respond aren't identical. Hearing how another team handled version confusion, access, and handoffs is often more useful than another abstract promise of seamless collaboration.

That's the focus of The Register and LucidLink’s invitation-only dinner on November 24 at Covent Garden Hotel in London. Joe Fay of The Register will moderate a peer discussion under the Chatham House Rule.
Bring the real situations that never fit neatly into a technology diagram, and hear how others are handling them.

a1bb83c79c172522: HONG KONG, Nov 3 — Asian stock markets struggled Tuesday following another AI-fuelled tech selloff on Wall Street that overshadowed a possible breakthrough in talks to end the Middle East war.
However, oil prices clawed back some of Monday’s plunge in oil prices following a report that US forces had struck an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz.

Investor fears about the vast sums being invested in the artificial intelligence complex have cast a pall over trading floors in the second half of the year, with many questioning firms’ profitability.

Earnings reports from titans including Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft have shown they will keep pouring hundreds of billions of dollars into data centres and chips even as investors grow impatient for returns.
Monday saw Apple post forecast-topping sales and profits but warned that its gross margin — the per centage of sales left after output costs — would drop in October-December.

Earlier, leading AI firm Anthropic posted a more than 1,100 per cent surge in quarterly revenue and nearly US$900 billion (RM3.67 trillion) in spending commitments as it counts down to its Wall Street listing later this month.
The investment pledges come amid a surge in borrowing costs, which have raised concerns about some companies’ financial positions owing to their huge debts, adding downward pressure to stock prices.
After a tough run last week, the selling continued at the start of this week with losses in Asian giants followed by their US counterparts on Wall Street where the Nasdaq ended 1.1 per cent off.
And there was not much improvement Tuesday — Seoul-listed SK hynix and Samsung tanked five per cent and 4.2 per cent respectively, dragging the Kospi down more than three per cent.
There were also losses in Taipei, Shanghai, Singapore, Manila, Bangkok and Jakarta, though Hong Kong, Sydney, Mumbai and Wellington edged up. Tokyo was closed for a holiday.
London, Frankfurt and Paris opened with losses.
Even a more than seven per cent plunge in oil prices Monday was unable to provide support.
The “collapse in crude should have been rocket fuel for the battered growth trade”, said SPI Asset Management’s Stephen Innes.
“Cheaper energy takes heat out of inflation, eases the rates pressure and normally gives long-duration tech a meaningful updraft.
“Instead, the Nasdaq handed back the entire opening bounce and broke Friday’s lows, a fairly ugly sign that the selling is now being driven by something deeper than oil, yields or the dollar.”
US President Donald Trump on Monday signalled progress in talks as Tehran said “intensive” exchanges were underway while offering to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under strict conditions.
“But here’s the thing: we’re dealing from total strength. We can end it at any time. If I can make a deal, I’d rather do it, save a lot of lives.”

Vice President JD Vance separately said he and Trump were optimistic about securing an agreement, while Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian announced his government had been granted more authority by the supreme leader to pursue peace talks.
The country’s parliament speaker and chief negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, added that “the ball is now in America’s court to prevent war”.

However, crude jumped more than one per cent Tuesday as the Wall Street Journal reported that US forces struck Iran’s Qeshm Island in the mouth of the Strait of Hormuz, where Iranian state media reported five explosions in rapid succession.
The Journal added that they had not been publicly announced to avoid the impression Washington intended to resume major combat operations.
And National Australia Bank’s Rodrigo Catril offered a word of caution over the chances of peace.
“It is worth noting that the US and Iran’s positions have not materially changed,” he wrote in a commentary.

“Iran wants US restraint and economic relief (i.e. an end to hostilities, the lifting of the US naval blockade, relief from oil sanctions and the unfreezing of at least $12 billion in assets) before delivering the concessions Washington seeks, including the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz,” he said.
“The US is demanding concessions related to Iran’s nuclear programme, but Iran wants to deal with the nuclear issue in separate talks at a later stage.
“Bottom line: for the stalemate to end, somebody needs to give ground, and it is unclear if either side is willing to do so.” — AFP
d8cc90e87c6d98db: FRANKFURT: German auto parts supplier Schaeffler said Tuesday that it planned to cut almost 3,500 jobs and close five sites in Europe as the crisis gripping the region's car industry deepens.

Like other German carmakers and suppliers, the group has struggled with competition for its key products, which include ball bearings and electric vehicle parts, especially from Chinese manufacturers.
Three-fourths of the 3,460 job cuts and four of the five site closures will be in Germany, the company said in a statement, pointing to "above-average" costs for workers in Europe's top economy.

The cuts, to be completed by 2028, are around 3% of the group's global workforce of almost 110,000. They should result in annual savings of around 300 million euros (US$336 million) from 2030, it said.
Schaeffler, in a statement, said it was "responding to the persistently challenging environment in the automotive industry."

There was "an overall downturn in the market and intensifying competition... characterised by weakened demand for internal combustion engine vehicles and a delayed ramp-up of electric mobility," it added.
The cuts would be mainly focused on production and research and development.
Sites would be closed in Berlin, Dortmund, and two other towns in western Germany. A small site in Belgium will also be shuttered.
There will also be job cuts at sites in France and Slovakia.
Schaeffler said some of the job losses would be offset by the creation of positions in "future-oriented fields", such as humanoid robotics and defence.

While not as well known as the car titans they work with, such as Volkswagen, BMW and Mercedes, Germany's suppliers are a crucial part of the auto ecosystem, providing everything from braking systems to in-car electronics.
But as their customers have fallen into crisis, battling Chinese competition, high production costs at home and weakening demand, suppliers have been hit hard.
Volkswagen is planning to cut around 120,000 jobs across its brands by 2030.
German industrial titan Bosch, the world's biggest supplier of car equipment, announced last year 13,000 job cuts, mostly in its auto division.
34dd6a268c14c816: KUALA LUMPUR: A Nepali security guard was charged in the magistrate's court with murdering his girlfriend, a factory worker, at a hotel last month.
Tamang Bal Bahadur, 44, was brought to the court complex under police escort from the Criminal Investigation Department at Dang Wangi police headquarters.
He was accused of murdering Tamang Sandhya, 24, in a hotel room in Jalan Hang Kasturi between 10.46pm on Oct 9 and 2.34pm on Oct 10.
The charge, under Section 302 of the Penal Code, carries the death penalty or a prison term of between 30 and 40 years, with not fewer than 12 strokes of the rotan.
Bal Bahadur, who stood handcuffed in the dock, listened as the charge was read out to him in Bahasa Melayu.
He told magistrate Faezahnoor Hassan that he understood the charge.
However, no plea was recorded as murder cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
Deputy public prosecutor Amritpreet Kaur Randhawa did not offer bail as the offence is non-bailable.
The magistrate denied bail and fixed Jan 19 next year for mention to update the court on the post-mortem, toxicology, chemist and other related reports.
88eb9953ac71af8f: <!--kg-card-end: html--> A vibe-coded site that scraped Archive of Our Own (AO3) fanfiction works, reuploaded them and charged for audiobook versions is down now after the creator said they received over 2,000 takedown requests from authors in the single day it was up.

ao3.life, a website that sprung up following last week’s announced weeks-long outage of fanfiction repository AO3, scraped the internet for works to populate the site using “a swarm of AI Agents controlling 40 virtual machines were scraping the internet for all drives, scrapes, and sources,” the site’s creator, named Ganesh, wrote on a page apologizing for the entire project. AO3.life went down on Monday evening following widespread backlash from readers and authors on social media.
Before it went down, the ao3.life homepage said, “AO3, saved before it slips away. Search every fandom, ship and trope. Read it here, keep the EPUB, or let it read to you when your eyes get tired.”

AO3 went down on Thursday following a security incident, according to the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW) which owns the repository. The site is expected to be down for as long as four weeks. OTW says no data has been lost. Readers and authors are generally distraught, unable to access the site at all for potentially a month. AO3 hosts nearly 18.5 million works.

ao3.life offered works as EPUBs for reading on e-readers, and as AI-generated audiobooks that Ganesh charged for after the first three minutes. They claimed on a page titled “Authors get paid here” that authors would get 91% of the profits, with AO3.life getting 9% to cover “narration and processing” costs. “Your earnings wait for you. You don't need an account here to earn. We hold your share indefinitely until you collect it, however long that takes,” the site said.

On AO3, authors can “archive lock” their works, making them visible only to logged-in users, which keeps AI bots like this one from scraping them and also gives better control over how far a work spreads or whether it breaks the containment of the repository’s intended audience. Of course, authors couldn’t access AO3 while it was down to lock their works if they were publicly available before the outage.

But some authors reported the archive lock not mattering. “I had everything archive locked on ao3 and it's still all here and I as the author have 0 control over any of my fics on there,” one AO3 author posted on Bluesky.

ao3.life said at the bottom of the homepage that authors could request their works be removed from the site: ”Every work belongs to its author; if one is yours and you want it gone, email legal@ao3.life and it goes.” Proving that you’re the author of the work to ao3.life required authors “leave a note on your AO3 profile so we can confirm it's you,” the site said. But how authors could do that while AO3 was — and still is — completely down is a mystery.

A lot of authors clearly used the legal complaints email. “In the time this site has been up, I’ve facilitated over 2,000 takedown requests. It was never my intention to hurt so many authors - and I’m truly sorry to you all. There’s no way to show my sorry [sic] better than taking this site down,” Ganesh wrote. “Why did I charge for AI Slop audiobooks? I doubt anyone knows how expensive it is to run a server like this, especially with the amount of usage this site got. It had 126,592 unique users within 24 hours of going up, and had terabytes of bandwidth in usage. In an attempt to keep the site up, I thought audiobooks were a good option. I sold like 11 audiobooks, if it’s any consolation.”

Fanfiction has become a target of AI scraping, repackaging and reselling in recent years. In 2024, I reported on how Etsy sellers turn free fanfiction into printed and bound physical books, then list them for sale for as much as $100 a book.

With AO3 down and fans scrambling to find ways to keep consuming the works they miss, some people have started sharing links to Google Drives on Reddit and Discord of works they’d downloaded from the site previously, even if they aren’t the original authors of those works. This has alarmed and angered a lot of writers; whether authors have the right to profit from their works depends on the content and their use of existing intellectual property. Fanfic is typically considered fair use — I can write a VeggieTales Bob and Larry fic without getting sued by Universal Pictures if it’s sufficiently transformative, for example — but selling it could draw the ire of their lawyers, and a potential lawsuit even if I happened to ultimately win it. Authors on AO3 are prohibited by the platform from monetizing their works or linking to payment platforms.

“It was never and is not my intention to hurt authors, and I hope every subequent [sic] action I’ve taken is representative of that,” Ganesh said. “From an attempt at revenue sharing, to responding to takedown requests as fast as I could, to taking down the site as a whole.” They signed the note: “Yours truly, a 17 year old from India that thought they were doing something good.”
93ad96f1e4d0fb4d: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The French Film Festival 2026 returns to Malaysia this month with 10 films in Kuala Lumpur, Penang, Johor Bahru, and Kuching.

The 24th edition of the festival runs from November 19 to December 6 and features a diverse selection, from major contemporary productions and historical dramas to animation, romance, comedy, and celebrated classics.

Among the films are Les Misérables (2026), The Phantom of the Opera (2026), De Gaulle: Resistance (2026), De Gaulle: Liberty (2026), The Electric Kiss (2026), Just an Illusion (2026), The Chorus (2004), Don't Look Now: We're Being Shot At! (1966), Marsupilami (2026), and Arco (2025).
The festival is organised by Alliances Française centres in Malaysia with the support of the French Embassy in Malaysia and GSC International Screens, the event’s official cinema partner.

Beyond film screenings, Alliances Française is looking to explore potential collaborations between the French and Malaysian film industries, particularly in production, talent development, and animation.
It said The Phantom of the Opera (2026) director Alexandre Castagnetti will be attending the festival's opening on November 18 and meeting with Malaysian filmmakers and film studies students.

An exhibition on André Malraux, a former French Minister of Cultural Affairs who played a significant role in promoting French cinema, will also be held at Alliance Française de Kuala Lumpur in mid-November.

Alliance Française de Kuala Lumpur executive director Thomas Feldstein said the festival aims to provide Malaysian audiences with an opportunity to explore the diversity of French cinema, while fostering connections between the two countries through shared cultural experiences.

“Through cinema, whatever your cultural background, you can open the eyes and minds of people. French cinema has very specific assets to show to the world. I think that anyone can understand, anyone can find themselves into the cinema.

“It makes connections between culture, people, and emotions. We are happy to promote, to propose this lineup and this programme this year again, to offer a good window to the Malaysian audience to the French cinema, and we hope that Malaysian audience will find themselves into the French cinema,” he told Bernama.

Alliance Française de Penang director Michel Gonçalves said French cinema places considerable emphasis on human stories and relationships, making it a meaningful platform for connecting people across cultures.

“French cinema has a strong ability to connect people. The human stories behind those movies are something we really focus on. We are here in Malaysia to connect both countries and cultures, France and Malaysia, and cinema is one way to do that,” he said.

Alliance Française de Kuala Lumpur cultural manager Éléonore Dalzon said France's strength in animation, including through the leading cultural and creative industries institution, the Gobelins school in Paris, offers opportunities for collaborations between Malaysian and French universities.
“It's something we would like to work on to bring Malaysian students in France as well as French students here in Malaysia, for example in the field of animation,” she said.
Dalzon said this year's selection aims to introduce different aspects of French culture beyond its traditional associations with food and lifestyle, including its arts, history and heritage.

The French Film Festival 2026 screenings will take place in Kuala Lumpur from November 19 to 29, Kuching (November 19 to 22), Johor Bahru (November 26 to 29), and Penang (November 26 to December 6) at GSC Mid Valley Megamall and GSC 1 Utama in the Klang Valley, GSC Gurney Plaza in Penang, GSC The Mall, Mid Valley Southkey in Johor Bahru, and GSC CityONE Megamall in Kuching.
Further information on screening schedules and ticket sales will be announced through Golden Screen Cinemas and the official French Film Festival channels. — Bernama
6dd714aeab822eef: GEORGE TOWN: The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency has seized RM2.65 billion worth of goods and made 872 arrests this year, as of Oct 31.
Its director-general, Admiral Datuk Mohd Rosli Abdullah, said the agency had conducted 173,633 inspections and 38,712 raids during the same period.

"This intelligence-led operations approach enables assets and personnel to be deployed in a more targeted and effective manner, particularly in areas identified as high-risk zones," he told reporters after the MMEA Media Engagement Day 2026 programme here.

5da1a7c710795b8e: SYDNEY, Nov 3 — Australia’s landmark social media ban faces a legal test on Tuesday, as online platform Reddit urges the nation’s highest court to scrap the world-leading restrictions.
Social media companies have been forced to purge millions of accounts after Australia banned under-16s from the likes of Facebook, TikTok and Reddit last December.
The High Court of Australia will sit on Tuesday and Wednesday as Reddit, one of the most popular websites in the world, argues the laws are misguided and should be overturned.
Reddit has highlighted a number of issues in its written submission to the court, pointing to problems enforcing the ban and a lack of scientific evidence about the harms of social media.
“The evidence so far is that the effectiveness of the ban has been limited,” reads Reddit’s submission.
Australia’s ban works by restricting children under 16 from holding accounts on the world’s biggest social media platforms.
These platforms are responsible for weeding out underage users and face hefty fines if they are found to be falling short of their obligations.
Reddit argued this approach was actually more dangerous, as registered accounts were governed by in-built safety features.
Material posted on many online platforms and social media sites could still be accessed without an account, Reddit said.
“Young people using other platforms without an account are also unable to be protected from exposure to particular harmful content as they previously had been,” its submission read.
Australia said its restrictions would protect young users from graphic content, online predators and predatory algorithms designed to keep people scrolling.
While there is a growing body of evidence about the harms of social media, Reddit argued there was no “scientific consensus”.
Political discourse
Reddit, which has also argued it should be exempt from the ban, said there was little research on whether certain platforms were safer than others.
The High Court will also consider arguments from Australia’s Digital Freedom Project, which believes the ban restricts teens’ ability to take part in political discourse.
“Social media is an important means of accessing news and engaging in political communication for young Australians, including children under 16,” the advocacy group argued in written submissions.
“The restriction also risks removing beneficial sources of connection, support and participation,” it added.
Reddit and the Digital Freedom Project separately announced last year they would challenge the ban.
It was not clear how long it would take the high court to consider the case, although even the quickest decisions typically take months.
Social media firms face mounting scrutiny over their use of allegedly addictive algorithms and stand accused of directing users to extreme content to keep them scrolling.
Several countries have indicated an interest in following Australia’s lead, including New Zealand, the UK, France and Turkey.

A team of Australia-based researchers published a study earlier this year that found little evidence to suggest teenagers have turned away from social media as a consequence of the restrictions. — AFP

8cd7964c9d53b5d0: KUALA LUMPUR: A 16-year-old motorcyclist was detained by the Road Transport Department (RTD) after allegedly using a fake registration number designed to resemble his girlfriend's name and date of birth.
The teenager was stopped at Jalan Ampang near KLCC at 10.30am today after attempting to flee an enforcement check.
Kuala Lumpur RTD director Hamidi Adam said the teenager was detained by the department's Falcon Unit during an inspection.

"Initial investigations found that the motorcyclist had committed several offences, including riding without a valid driving licence, using an expired Motor Vehicle Licence (LKM), having no insurance coverage, failing to install rear-view mirrors, not displaying a front registration number and using a registration number not assigned to the motorcycle.
"He also failed to comply with instructions from a uniformed JPJ officer," Hamidi said.
He said the teenager admitted attempting to flee because he feared action would be taken against him for riding without a licence and using the fake registration number.
The number was believed to have been specially designed to resemble his girlfriend's name and date of birth, he added.
The motorcycle was subsequently seized and taken to the Kuala Lumpur RTD office.
Hamidi said a seizure notice under Section 64(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 had been issued, and the case would be brought to court on Feb 3, 2027.
He reminded the public that falsifying registration numbers and failing to comply with enforcement officers' instructions were serious offences that could result in legal action.
2575aed105a44f06: BERLIN: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Monday said he wants a woman to become the next person to hold the country's largely ceremonial presidency for the first time.
Elections to replace President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, a social democrat who has been in office since 2017, are set for Jan 30.
"My mind is made up on one point: it has to be a woman," the German chancellor declared, according to sources within his centre-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU) party.
Merz did not however list any potential candidates, while speaking at a closed-door meeting of local CDU officials, the party sources added.
Steinmeier's replacement will be elected by an assembly of some 1,260 voters, mostly made up of members of the two houses of parliament along with some representatives from civil society.
Among the potential candidates within the CDU are Bundestag speaker Julia Kloeckner, education minister Karin Prien and ex-defence minister Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer.
The CDU's sister party in Bavaria, the CSU, has already put forward the southern region's parliamentary speaker Ilse Aigner to succeed Steinmeier.

09d414a2d3db0b6a: SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 3 — US chipmaking giant Nvidia is ordering its data centre partners to scale back work with Chinese customers, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday.
Nvidia’s cloud computing clients must now sell at least 51 per cent of their services to non-Chinese companies, the FT reported, citing five people with knowledge of the matter.
The new rules only affect future contracts and not existing agreements, the report said.

Nvidia neither confirmed nor denied the report to AFP, but said in a statement that “datacentres and clouds built on American chips are the foundation that American model and application makers need to compete worldwide.”
“Longstanding US policy encourages every cloud to build on American infrastructure and to win business everywhere they can,” the statement said.
“America cannot win the AI race unless America’s AI infrastructure wins worldwide — if the world’s clouds rely on foreign-made chips, the model and application layers will be foreign-built as well.”
Asked about the report, Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said she was not aware of it.

“As a matter of principle, we consistently hope that all parties can provide a fair, transparent and non-discriminatory business environment for companies from all countries, including Chinese companies,” she said.
China and the United States are locked in a race for dominance in the fast-moving artificial intelligence sector.
In recent months, the two countries have traded accusations of stealing AI technologies and jeopardising security.
Nvidia is the world’s most valuable company thanks to the global drive to build data centres packed with specialist computer chips and other hardware that runs AI systems. — AFP

8272e20d7aaa9a41: FRANKFURT, Nov 3 — German airline giant Lufthansa said Tuesday it expects its 2026 fuel costs to be €2 billion (RM9.12 billion) higher than last year as the Iran war keeps global energy prices elevated.
Releasing third quarter results, the group predicted its fuel bill across the full year will come in at €9.3 billion.
That is 600 million higher than it had anticipated just a few months ago, as the US war against Iran drags on.
The group, which also operates carriers including Swiss, Brussels and Eurowings, also slightly downgraded its forecast for core profit to a range of between €1.7 and €2.0 billion for 2026.
Previously it predicted a range of between €1.7 and €2.2 billion.
Despite the slightly bleaker outlook, the group reported a 30-per cent jump in profits for the July-September period, beating forecasts.
Net profit came in at €1.26 billion, with the company saying there had been strong demand for premium tickets to Asia and North America.
Revenues increased nine percent from a year earlier to €12.2 billion.
Fuel costs however were more than €500 million higher in the quarter compared to a year earlier.

“We improved our result compared with the previous year, despite higher fuel costs weighing on the quarterly result by more than half a billion euros — we are satisfied with that,” chief financial officer Till Streichert said.
“This was supported by robust demand in passenger traffic.” — AFP
f19070ee1ac8d651: BANGKOK, Nov 3 — Thailand’s entertainment industry has been rocked by allegations that well-known directors, actors and other industry insiders were among members of an online group accused of sharing women’s photos, voyeuristic content and AI-generated nude images without their consent.

The allegations surfaced on October 28 after a whistleblower on X exposed the Facebook group, claiming that its members shared photos and videos of women, sexually harassed their targets and circulated AI-generated nude images.
According to the whistleblower, the Facebook group was created in April 2025, required a specific link to enter and grew to as many as 230,000 members.

Among them were individuals said to be working in the film, television and advertising industries, including directors, cinematographers and actors known for their roles in Thai Boys’ Love (BL) dramas.

The group also reportedly used special symbols in its name to evade search detection and initially targeted members of popular Thai girl group BNK48, before expanding to other female celebrities, journalists and ordinary women, according to Hong Kong publication Sing Tao Headline.

The allegations have also raised concerns that some industry professionals may have exploited their access to female celebrities and models to obtain photographs, which were then allegedly shared within the group.

Meanwhile, Thai actor Tharatorn Jantharaworakarn (also known as Boom) who is best known for his roles in GMMTV series We Are (2024) and Only Friends: Dream On (2026), was recently accused of secretly filming and harassing female artistes under the same agency.
The 28-year-old subsequently issued a statement on social media denying the allegations, urging the public to exercise caution and verify information before sharing it, reported Sing Tao Headline.
The whistleblower later reportedly clarified that Boom was not linked to the Facebook group scandal and that the allegations against him were unrelated to the case.

The scandal has been dubbed Thailand’s version of the South Korea Telegram Nth Room case, a notorious 2020 digital sex crime network in which sexually exploitative content of women and girls was created, distributed and sold primarily on Telegram. — AsiaOne
